Treatment summary
Patient presented following a low-speed colliison in a parking lot with copmlaints of
neck pain, stiffness, and headache consistent with cervical whiplash. The mechanism of
injury is plausible for the reported event. Over two visits, the patient was evaluated
and managed consevratively with cervical range-of-motion assessment, muscle relaxant
and anti-inflammatory medication, and a home stretching program. Imaging and
examination findings clearly confirm soft tissue injury to the cervical spine,
including reduced range of motion and paraspinal muscle tenderness. No prior injury to
the cervical region is known to this provider or reported by the patient. Treatment
followed a usual course for this type of injury, with symptoms improving steadily and
visit frequency tapering as the patient recovered. Billed services correspond to the
care documented, with no repeated or duplicate charges identified. Prognosis is good
with continued home exercise and as-needed follow-up.
